title: Compton's 1923 quantum theory of X-ray scattering
summary: Arthur H. Compton proposed in Physical Review in May 1923 that an X-ray quantum gives all its energy and momentum to a single electron, so the scattered ray has a longer wavelength that does not depend on the incident wavelength.
body: In *Physical Review* 21(5), May 1923, pages 483–502, Arthur H. Compton proposed that an incident X-ray quantum transfers all its energy and momentum to one electron, which recoils. He wrote that a quantum "spends all of its energy and momentum upon some particular electron", and derived a scattered-wavelength increase of (2h/mc) sin²(θ/2) = 0.0484 sin²(θ/2) Å, adding that "the increase is independent of the wave-length." The abstract reports unpublished measurements for graphite with Mo-K radiation giving a shift of .022 Å against a computed .024 Å. Compton states that the agreement between experiment and theory "indicates clearly that scattering is a quantum phenomenon".

sources.title: A Quantum Theory of the Scattering of X-rays by Light Elements
sources.author: Arthur H. Compton
